expectations.text: service_graph_chain(PA then F5 ordering with rationale)
expectations.evidence: SGT_INBOUND_CHAIN defines Node1: PA5400_FW -> Node2: F5_LB with L3 adjacency. Rationale: PA inspects/decrypts first, F5 load balances after. Detailed service graph template with connections C1->C2->C3 in Ansible playbook.
Section 5 details Active/Passive HA with dedicated HA1 (eth1/5, control) and HA2 (eth1/6, state sync), election priority 100/90, preemption disabled, aggressive timers, link+path monitoring.

Three zones defined: OUTSIDE (ae1, zone protection ZP_OUTSIDE with SYN cookies/flood/recon protection), DMZ (ae2, ZP_DMZ), MGMT. Six ordered security rules including OUTSIDE->DMZ allow HTTPS, DMZ->OUTSIDE deny, and implicit deny-all.

Section 7 details SSL Inbound Inspection mode using server private key. Decryption profiles SSLPROF_INBOUND_WEB/API with TLS 1.2-1.3. Decryption policy rules DECRYPT_INBOUND_HTTPS/API targeting VIPs. Certificate store with wildcard and api certs, HSM storage, renewal via Ansible. Capacity planning table included.

VS_DMZ_WEB_HTTPS (10.1.2.10:443) with clientssl profile, tcp-wan/lan-optimized, HTTP with XFF, compression, iRules. POOL_WEB_SERVERS with least-connections, MON_HTTP_WEB (GET /health, expect 200). VS_DMZ_API_HTTPS (10.1.2.11:443) with POOL_API_SERVERS and MON_HTTPS_API. SSL profiles with TLS1.2+ and ECDHE+AESGCM ciphers.
Section 6 specifies Active/Standby HA with Device Trust Group DG_DMZ_F5, network failover, connection mirroring, auto-failback disabled. Dedicated HA VLAN 4094 with self-IPs 169.254.1.1/2.

Three PBR policies defined: PBR_TO_PA_OUTSIDE (10.1.1.10, backup 10.1.1.11), PBR_PA_INSIDE_TO_F5_EXTERNAL (10.1.2.10, backup 10.1.2.11), PBR_F5_INTERNAL_TO_SERVERS (not required with SNAT). Resilient hashing and threshold tracking enabled. Full Ansible vnsSvcRedirectPol tasks included.

Section 8 defines CON_WEB_TO_API (tcp/8443,443,dns), CON_API_TO_APP (tcp/8443,50051,dns), CON_APP_TO_DB (tcp/3306,5432,6379) with explicit consumer/provider EPGs. Implicit deny for all non-contracted paths. Intra-EPG isolation enforced on DB tier. VRF enforcement enabled with preferred group disabled.

Section 3 provides 11-step inbound flow: Client->L3Out on Leaf-01/02->EPG_OUTSIDE->CON_INTERNET_TO_DMZ->PBR to PA outside->PA inspection/decryption->PA inside->PBR to F5 external->F5 VIP processing->F5 internal->EPG_WEB_TIER. East-west Web->API->App->DB via microsegmentation contracts.

Section 9 lists all three collections in requirements.yml: cisco.aci >=2.8.0, paloaltonetworks.panos >=2.17.0, f5networks.f5_modules >=1.25.0. Full playbooks using cisco.aci.aci_rest, paloaltonetworks.panos.panos_security_rule/panos_decryption_rule/panos_nat_rule, f5networks.f5_modules.bigip_as3_deploy.

expectations.text: monitoring_health_scores(ACI health scores+PA threat logs+F5 pool health)
expectations.evidence: Section 10 details ACI EPG health scores via REST API (alert <90), service graph health, PBR redirect health. PA threat detections via syslog (type=threat), HA state, session counts. F5 pool member health via validation playbook. Grafana dashboards and PagerDuty alerting.

expectations.text: device_package_registration(ACI device package for PA and/or F5)
expectations.evidence: Section 4 registers both devices as L4-L7 logical devices: PA5400_HA_CLUSTER (svcType FW, unmanaged, GoTo, with CDev_PA_A/B concrete devices and outside/inside interfaces) and F5_BIGIP_HA_CLUSTER (svcType ADC, unmanaged, GoTo, with CDev_F5_ACTIVE/STANDBY). Full Ansible tasks using vnsLDevVip with concrete device children.
